newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo Met Mining to cut copper, zinc in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo Met Mining to cut copper, zinc in 2nd half.

text.p: Sumitomo Metal Mining Co said on Friday it plans modest cuts in copper and zinc output in the half year to next March from the year-ago period, but expects lead and nickel/ferronickel output to rise.
Copper output will dip to 105,300 tonnes from 105,799 tonnes in a year earlier, but will be unchanged from originally planned output of 105,300 tonnes in April-September 1996.

Zinc production is expected to fall to 52,300 tonnes from year-ago output of 54,875 tonnes, although it will be higher than the planned 39,500 tonnes for April-September 1996, when the Harima smelter was shut for scheduled maintenance.
Lead output will rise to 13,300 tonnes from 11,753 tonnes in the year-ago period and output of 11,500 tonnes it had planned for April-September.
Nickel and ferronickel output is planned at 23,600 tonnes, up from 22,128 tonnes in the same period a year before and the planned April-September level of 23,500 tonnes.
Gold output will increase to 13.0 tonnes from 11.795 tonnes in the same period a year earlier, and silver to 114.8 tonnes from 106.177 tonnes.
The data includes copper tolled for another refining firm.
